Toasted Dulse Crisps

Served at: Imbolc Day Celebration

Serves 4-6Prep 5 minCook 5-10 min

Dulse, an edible red seaweed, offers a unique umami flavor and a wealth of minerals, making it a nourishing choice as we transition from winter's depths to the promise of spring at Imbolc. These simple, crispy dulse snacks celebrate the earth's bounty and provide a light, wholesome bite perfect for a seasonal gathering, symbolizing renewal and simple sustenance.

Ingredients

  • 1 ounce (28g) dried dulse flakes or whole leaves
  • 1 tablespoon (15ml) olive oil or neutral oil
  • Pinch of sea salt (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 300°F (150°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. If using whole dulse leaves, gently break them into bite-sized pieces. If using flakes, they are ready as is.
  3. In a medium bowl, toss the dulse with the olive oil until lightly coated.
  4. Spread the dulse in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
  5. Bake for 5-10 minutes, or until the dulse is crispy and slightly darkened, but not burnt. Keep a close eye on it, as it can burn quickly.
  6. Remove from the oven and, if desired, sprinkle with a pinch of sea salt while still warm.
  7. Let cool completely before serving. The crisps will become even crispier as they cool.

Tips

  • For a smoky flavor, add a tiny dash of smoked paprika or a few drops of liquid smoke mixed with the oil before tossing.
  • Serve these crisps as a healthy snack, a garnish for soups or salads, or alongside a cheese board.
  • Store any leftover crisps in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days to maintain their crispness.
